<!-- pr-reviewer: 5c6573102489426732decd3fb6a106a59403d904 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good:
- The two-level table (q379 / q208) matches the research: `differences.md` B2/B3 rows (Q395 only from iTNC 60642x-04, TNC 640 34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01, TNC 320 77185x-01; Q379/Q253 from iTNC 340 422 and the other controls; the 340 49x cycle examples end without Q395/Q208) and `dialects.md` (`itnc-49x` vs `itnc-60642x-04`; TNC 640 `tnc640-a` vs `tnc640-b`; TNC 620 `tnc620-mid`/`tnc620-early` vs `tnc620-81760x`; TNC 320 `tnc320-early`/`tnc320-34055x` vs `tnc320-77185x`). The refusal for a stated control outside the table (e.g. iTNC 530 340 420, TNC 640 34059x-03, TNC7) follows `dialects.md` ("An unknown model or a version outside the table: the post refuses by name").
- Only Q208 and Q395 are dropped at level q379: the rest of the G200/G205 word set (Q200/Q201/Q202/Q203/Q204/Q206/Q210/Q211/Q212/Q205/Q256/Q257/Q258/Q259/Q379/Q253) is pushed unchanged, and the no-identity output is word-order-identical to today's (verified against origin/main: the words and their arguments are the same, and the existing no-identity pinning test stays green).
- The two refusal paths are by name: an unknown control/version is refused in `drillLevel()` before any block is emitted; an ask the old cycle cannot take is refused by name in the guard (`G205 Q208=500 cannot be written ...`), never dropped silently. The guard compares with a fixed `OLD_CYCLE_RETRACT_FEED` constant, so a script variant that changes `RETRACT_FEED_MAX` cannot hide the mismatch.
- The new pins are in the existing `heidenhain_cycles` binary (`crates/post/tests/heidenhain_cycles/levels.rs` via `#[path = "heidenhain_cycles/levels.rs"] mod levels;`), not a new test binary. The Gate map line is updated to name `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps`.
- The "goldens moved: none" claim holds: `git diff origin/main...5c657310 --stat` shows no golden files, and the heidenhain golden tests post on the identity-less generic VMC (`3axis-vmc.mch`), which keeps the no-identity output unchanged (the post- and example_catalog suites pass).
- The decision file is present and records the no-identity fallback and the fixed-constant guard fix.

Results (all local, worktree `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4172-review` off head `5c6573102`):
- Trial merge with `origin/main` (12ea01a45): clean, nothing to merge (`git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main` -> "Already up to date").
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test heidenhain_cycles`: 16 passed, 0 failed (5 levels tests green: Picomax 340490-03, before/from-the-q208-level tables, unknown control refusal, Q208-ask refusal).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 43 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`) was not run by this reviewer; the PR body cites the author's run (6 steps, 0 failed). No heavy lane is owed for this PR (P3, not a wrong-output change to a mechanism under the safety floor).
- No wind-up: not run on the runner (local review, no runner used).

Requested before merge: none.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
1. 73498x releases past the documented range (-03 and up) and 34056x releases past -04 are treated as q379 by `drillLevel()` rather than refused. The dialects.md table ends at `tnc620-mid` = `340 56x-02 … 73498x-02`, so a 34056x-05 or 73498x-03 would post with the q379 set instead of the named refusal. No shipped machine file carries such a version and the behavior is the conservative guess, so this is a note, not a blocker; the #4095 resolver can tighten the table.
2. The refusal happens inside `onCycle` before the block is emitted; a stream with present-but-unsupported controls fails the whole program. That is the documented contract ("refused, not posted") and matches the existing refusal style.
3. The `drillLevel()` helper is a table keyed on model+NC software; it is intentionally structured for #4095 to replace. The comment in the post says so.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: e20797ba437f210cf58008e0e54cbd7bbbfd509b -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good:
- Commit `e20797ba4` closes finding 1 of the safety-tier review of head `5c6573102`. The post no longer matches a prefix of the NC software string. It parses the complete canonical identifier (`^(\d{5})(\d)-(\d{2})(?: SP[1-9]\d{0,2})?$`) and then requires one row of `DRILL_ROWS` to match the model, the family, the variant range (iTNC 530 34049 + `0..4`, 60642 + `0..5`, 340 422 only variant 2, the TNC 640/620/320 families `0..5`) and a release that the research names (never `-00`). Anything else is refused by name (`the cycle 200/205 parameter set of <model> NC <nc> is not known to this post - refused, not posted`), before any block is emitted.
- The table is faithful to `docs/research/heidenhain/differences.md` B2/B3 and `dialects.md`: iTNC 530 34049x `-01..-08` and 60642x `-01..-03` are q379; 60642x-04 (+SP8) is q208; TNC 640 34059x `-04..-11` and `-16..-18` are q208 (B3 has no `-12..-15` example); TNC 620 81760x `-01..-08` and `-16..-18` are q208 (B3 has no `-09..-15`); TNC 620 34056x `-01..-04` and 73498x `-01/-02` are q379; TNC 320 34055x `-01..-06` are q379; TNC 320 77185x `-01,-02,-04,-05,-06,-18` are q208; iTNC 530 340 422 (any release) is q379.
- The regression test `a_malformed_or_unsupported_nc_identifier_is_refused_by_name` covers malformed suffixes (`340490-03junk`, `340490-030`, `340490-3`, `340490-03 sp8`, `606425-04 SP`, `606425-04 SP0`, `606425-04SP8`), zero and unnamed releases (`340490-00`, `340490-09`, `606425-05`, `340595-12`, `817600-00`), unsupported variants (`340499-03`, `340495-03`, `606426-04`, `340421-02`) and a valid identifier under the wrong model (`TNC 640` with `340490-03`). The valid rows also gain `340490-03`, `340494-05`, `606425-04 SP8`, `340595-11` and `817600-18`.
- The earlier note about TNC 620 73498x/34056x releases above the documented range is resolved: `-03` and later are refused by name, not guessed as q379.
- The new test file is a submodule of the existing `heidenhain_cycles` binary (`crates/post/tests/heidenhain_cycles/levels.rs` via the `#[path]` mod), with no new top-level test binary, and the Gate map line names `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps`.
- The no-identity output stays unchanged: no golden changed (the goldens post on the identity-less generic `3axis-vmc.mch`), and the existing no-identity pinning test still passes. The refusal of an ask the old cycle cannot take (G205 Q208=500) is still pinned with a script variant that changes `RETRACT_FEED_MAX`, and the guard now compares against a fixed `OLD_CYCLE_RETRACT_FEED`.
- The decision file records the strict parse, the variant/release ranges, the dropped open bound and the no-identity fallback. The body ends `Fixes #4094`, has a `Changelog:` line, and the commits are conventional.

Results (on the self-hosted runner, run <https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/45848566868>, PR head `e20797ba4`, merged against main `e6849c5ae`):
- Trial merge with main: clean (the workflow merged and built the merged tree; main does not touch the four changed files).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on the merged tree: 220 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (18.8 min wall). Includes the post suites: `heidenhain_cycles` (17 tests) and the app suites `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (no warnings; `Finished`).
- No failure text: the run conclusion is `success`.
- The light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`) was not run locally: the machine is heavily loaded (another review runs a light lane), and the release build exceeded the 10-minute per-command cap on two attempts, so the run was stopped rather than left to die silently. It is also not owed by this PR: the diff touches only `camcraft-post` (the post script, one test submodule and the decision file), never a heavy-lane crate (`kernel`/`motion`/`app`). The author's body cites a green light run on this head (6 steps, 0 failed, macOS). The result stands as a note, not a pass.
- The example catalog suites (the only app suites the diff can change: the post script) ran green on the runner.
- No heavy step is owed (P3, not a wrong-output change under the safety floor). No `<!-- heavy-wave -->` record was cited and none is owed.

Requested before merge: none.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
1. `q208` at the TNC 640/620/320 `-16..-18` rows writes Q208/Q395 without Q373, which the research names for those releases (TNC 640/620 `-16` and later, TNC 320 771851-18, TNC7). The decision file records this as out of scope (#4095): the controls keep the output of today, which is q208. Reasonable as a conservative level; the #4095 resolver can write Q373.
2. The refusal happens inside `onCycle` before any block is emitted, so one refused cycle suppresses the whole program's cycle blocks. This matches the documented "refused, not posted" contract.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
